column1: Educating Psyche by Bernie Neville is a book which looks at radical new approaches to learning, describing the effects of emotion, imagination and the unconscious on learning.
column2: 伯尼·内维尔在《心智教育》一书中探讨了突破常规的学习方法，并阐述了情感、想象力和无意识对学习的影响。

column1: One theory discussed in the book is that proposed by George Lozanov, which focuses on the power of suggestion.
column2: 书中讨论的理论之一由乔治·洛扎诺夫提出，着重探讨暗示的力量。

column1: Lozanov’s instructional technique is based on the evidence that the connections made in the brain through unconscious processing (which he calls non-specific mental reactivity) are more durable than those made through conscious processing.
column2: 洛扎诺夫的教学方法有这样的证据作为依据：大脑通过无意识加工（他称之为“非特异性心理反应”）建立的联系，比通过有意识加工建立的联系更为持久。
column8: non-specific mental reactivity|非特异性心理反应

column1: Besides the laboratory evidence for this, we know from our experience that we often remember what we have perceived peripherally, long after we have forgotten what we set out to learn.
column2: 除了实验室的证据，我们自己也有这样的体验：原先想学的东西早已忘记，无意间注意到的细节却常常还记得。
column6: perceived peripherally|在注意力未集中的情况下察觉到

column1: If we think of a book we studied months or years ago, we will find it easier to recall peripheral details - the colour, the binding, the typeface, the table at the library where we sat while studying it - than the content on which we were concentrating.
column2: 回想几个月或几年前研读过的一本书，我们会发现，较容易回忆起来的是一些次要细节，例如书的颜色、装帧、字体，还有我们在图书馆读这本书时坐的那张桌子。相比之下，当时专心研读的内容反而更难回想。

column1: If we think of a lecture we listened to with great concentration, we will recall the lecturer’s appearance and mannerisms, our place in the auditorium, the failure of the air-conditioning, much more easily than the ideas we went to learn.
column2: 回想一场我们曾全神贯注听过的讲座，讲者的外貌和习惯动作、我们在听众席上的座位，以及空调出了故障这些事，都比我们原本想从中学到的观点更容易回忆起来。
column11: much more easily than|比……容易得多

column1: Even if these peripheral details are a bit elusive, they come back readily in hypnosis or when we relive the event imaginatively, as in psychodrama.
column2: 即使这些无关主旨的细节有些难以回想，在催眠状态下，或在想象中重温当时的情景时（如在心理剧中），它们也很容易重新浮现。

column1: The details of the content of the lecture, on the other hand, seem to have gone forever.
column2: 相比之下，讲座内容的细节却仿佛再也想不起来了。
column5: on the other hand|相比之下

column1: This phenomenon can be partly attributed to the common counterproductive approach to study (making extreme efforts to memorise, tensing muscles, inducing fatigue), but it also simply reflects the way the brain functions.
column2: 这种现象部分可以归因于一种常见却适得其反的学习方法（拼命记忆、绷紧肌肉，因而感到疲劳），但它也只是反映了大脑本身的运作方式。

column1: Lozanov therefore made indirect instruction (suggestion) central to his teaching system.
column2: 因此，洛扎诺夫把间接教学（即暗示）置于其教学体系的核心。
column6: central to|在……中居于核心地位

column1: In suggestopedia, as he called his method, consciousness is shifted away from the curriculum to focus on something peripheral.
column2: 洛扎诺夫把这种方法称为“暗示教学法”。在这种方法中，学生把有意识的注意力从课程内容转向某个与课程关系不大的事物。
column9: peripheral|adj. 处于注意焦点之外的

column1: The curriculum then becomes peripheral and is dealt with by the reserve capacity of the brain.
column2: 这样，课程内容就退到了注意力之外，由大脑的储备能力来处理。
column4: peripheral|adj. 处于注意焦点之外的
column6: reserve capacity|n. 储备能力；未充分利用的能力

column1: The suggestopedic approach to foreign language learning provides a good illustration.
column2: 外语学习中的暗示教学法就是一个很好的例子。
column3: suggestopedic|adj. 采用暗示教学法的
column5: foreign language learning|n. 外语学习

column1: In its most recent variant (1980), it consists of the reading of vocabulary and text while the class is listening to music.
column2: 在当时最新的版本（1980年）里，学生听着音乐，教师同时朗读词汇和课文。
column4: variant|n. 变体；这里指不同版本

column1: The first session is in two parts.
column2: 第一节课分为两部分。

column1: In the first part, the music is classical (Mozart, Beethoven, Brahms) and the teacher reads the text slowly and solemnly, with attention to the dynamics of the music.
column2: 第一部分播放古典音乐（莫扎特、贝多芬、勃拉姆斯的作品），教师缓慢、庄重地朗读课文，留意乐曲的强弱变化。

column1: The students follow the text in their books.
column2: 学生看着书，跟随教师的朗读默读课文。
column3: follow the text|跟着朗读看课文
column4: in their books|在各自的书上

column1: This is followed by several minutes of silence.
column2: 接下来是几分钟的静默。

column1: In the second part, they listen to baroque music (Bach, Corelli, Handel) while the teacher reads the text in a normal speaking voice.
column2: 第二部分播放巴洛克音乐（巴赫、科雷利、亨德尔的作品），同时教师用平时说话的声音朗读课文。
column6: normal speaking voice|n. 平时说话的声音

column1: During this time they have their books closed.
column2: 在这段时间里，学生一直合着书。
column3: During this time|在这段时间里
column4: have their books closed|让书一直合着

column1: During the whole of this session, their attention is passive; they listen to the music but make no attempt to learn the material.
column2: 整节课上，学生都处于被动接收的状态：他们听音乐，却不刻意去学教材内容。
column3: During the whole of|在整个……期间

column1: Beforehand, the students have been carefully prepared for the language learning experience.
column2: 上课之前，学生已经在细致的引导下为这次语言学习做好了准备。
column4: have been carefully prepared for|已得到细致引导，为……做好准备
column5: language learning experience|n. 语言学习体验

column1: Through meeting with the staff and satisfied students they develop the expectation that learning will be easy and pleasant and that they will successfully learn several hundred words of the foreign language during the class.
column2: 通过和教职人员及对课程满意的学生见面，他们开始期待，学习会轻松愉快，而且自己能在一节课上学会几百个外语单词。

column1: In a preliminary talk, the teacher introduces them to the material to be covered, but does not ‘teach’ it.
column2: 在课前谈话中，教师向学生介绍将要学习的材料，但并不实际“教”这些内容。
column6: to be covered|v. 将要讲到的

column1: Likewise, the students are instructed not to try to learn it during this introduction.
column2: 同样，教师也告诉学生，在这段介绍过程中不必刻意去学这些材料。
column4: are instructed not to|被告知不要……

column1: Some hours after the two-part session, there is a follow-up class at which the students are stimulated to recall the material presented.
column2: 两部分课程结束几小时后，还有一堂后续课，教师会引导学生回想先前接触的内容。
column3: two-part session|n. 分为两部分的课
column7: material presented|n. 先前呈现的学习材料

column1: Once again the approach is indirect.
column2: 这一次，教学方式仍是间接的。

column1: The students do not focus their attention on trying to remember the vocabulary, but focus on using the language to communicate (e.g. through games or improvised dramatisations).
column2: 学生把注意力放在用所学语言交流上（例如做游戏或即兴表演），而不刻意去回忆词汇。
column3: focus their attention on|把注意力集中在……上

column1: Such methods are not unusual in language teaching.
column2: 这类方法在语言教学中并不少见。

column1: What is distinctive in the suggestopedic method is that they are devoted entirely to assisting recall.
column2: 暗示教学法的独特之处在于，这些活动完全是为了帮助学生回忆所学内容。
column5: are devoted entirely to|完全用于……

column1: The ‘learning’ of the material is assumed to be automatic and effortless, accomplished while listening to music.
column2: 这种教学法认为，对材料的“学习”在听音乐时就自动完成了，不用刻意费力。
column5: is assumed to be|被认为是

column1: The teacher’s task is to assist the students to apply what they have learned paraconsciously, and in doing so to make it easily accessible to consciousness.
column2: 教师的任务是帮助学生运用在意识之外学到的知识，从而使他们能够轻松地、有意识地调用这些知识。
column6: paraconsciously|adv. 在意识之外地（指学习过程）
column8: accessible to consciousness|能被有意识地调取

column1: Another difference from conventional teaching is the evidence that students can regularly learn 1000 new words of a foreign language during a suggestopedic session, as well as grammar and idiom.
column2: 与常规教学相比，还有一点不同：有证据表明，学生在一节暗示教学课上常常能学会一千个外语生词，外加语法和习语。

column1: Lozanov experimented with teaching by direct suggestion during sleep, hypnosis and trance states, but found such procedures unnecessary.
column2: 洛扎诺夫曾尝试在睡眠、催眠和恍惚状态下以直接暗示进行教学，但他发现这些做法并无必要。

column1: Hypnosis, yoga, Silva mind-control, religious ceremonies and faith healing are all associated with successful suggestion, but none of their techniques seem to be essential to it.
column2: 催眠、瑜伽、席尔瓦心灵控制法、宗教仪式和信仰疗法都与成功的暗示有关，但其中似乎没有哪种技巧是暗示起效所必需的。
column7: are all associated with|都与……有关

column1: Such rituals may be seen as placebos.
column2: 这类仪式可以看作安慰剂。
column4: may be seen as|可以被看作

column1: Lozanov acknowledges that the ritual surrounding suggestion in his own system is also a placebo, but maintains that without such a placebo people are unable or afraid to tap the reserve capacity of their brains.
column2: 洛扎诺夫承认，他自己的体系中，伴随暗示而来的仪式也是一种安慰剂，但他坚持认为，缺少这种安慰剂，人们就不能或不敢动用大脑的储备能力。
column8: unable or afraid to|不能或不敢……

column1: Like any placebo, it must be dispensed with authority to be effective.
column2: 和任何安慰剂一样，这种仪式也得由施行者带着权威感来实施，才能奏效。

column1: Just as a doctor calls on the full power of autocratic suggestion by insisting that the patient take precisely this white capsule precisely three times a day before meals, Lozanov is categoric in insisting that the suggestopedic session be conducted exactly in the manner designated, by trained and accredited suggestopedic teachers.
column2: 正如医生会充分借助权威式暗示的力量，坚称患者必须服用的就是这种白色胶囊，每天恰好三次，而且要在餐前服用，洛扎诺夫也明确坚持，暗示教学课必须严格依照指定方式，由受过培训且取得资格的暗示教学法教师来上。
column9: three times a day|每天三次
column15: trained and accredited|受过培训并取得资格的
column16: suggestopedic teachers|n. 使用暗示教学法的教师

column1: While suggestopedia has gained some notoriety through success in the teaching of modern languages, few teachers are able to emulate the spectacular results of Lozanov and his associates.
column2: 暗示教学法虽然因在现代语言教学中取得成功而颇受瞩目，但很少有教师能取得洛扎诺夫及其同事那样引人注目的成效。
column8: emulate|v. 努力达到与……相同的水平

column1: We can, perhaps, attribute mediocre results to an inadequate placebo effect.
column2: 效果平平，或许是因为安慰剂效应不够强。
column5: mediocre results|n. 平平的教学效果

column1: The students have not developed the appropriate mind set.
column2: 学生还没有形成适合这种学习方法的心态。

column1: They are often not motivated to learn through this method.
column2: 他们往往缺乏采用这种方法学习的动力。
column4: not motivated to|缺乏做……的动力
column5: through this method|通过这种方法

column1: They do not have enough ‘faith’.
column2: 他们对这种方法缺少足够的“信心”。

column1: They do not see it as ‘real teaching’, especially as it does not seem to involve the ‘work’ they have learned to believe is essential to learning.
column2: 他们不把这当作“真正的教学”，尤其是因为这种方法似乎不要求他们付出那种他们一向认为学习必需的“功夫”。
column6: work|n. 为学习付出的功夫
